title: Map of Antarctica: routes to the South Pole
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y6 lesson 9 (Map of Antarctica with the Ross Ice Shelf (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 9. Trace Amundsen's and Scott's routes (1911 to 1912) and label the bases, the Ross Ice Shelf, the glaciers, the plateau and the Pole.

blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: Describe the first stage of both routes.
questions.a: Crossing the flat Ross Ice Shelf southwards
questions.model: Look at the map. Both bases are on the coast. Both went south across the Ross Ice Shelf first.

questions.q: Why is the polar plateau hard to cross?
questions.a: It is high, very cold and windy

questions.q: Core: On a map of Antarctica, trace both routes and label the bases, the ice shelf, the glaciers, the plateau and the Pole.
questions.a: Both routes from the coast across the Ross Ice Shelf, up a glacier, across the plateau to the Pole, with labels
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: dot the Bay of Whales, draw Amundsen's line south across the ice shelf, label 'Ross Ice Shelf'.

questions.q: Extend: Describe Amundsen's route in three sentences using compass directions.
questions.a: For example: He set off south from the Bay of Whales across the Ross Ice Shelf. He climbed the Axel Heiberg Glacier onto the plateau. He travelled south to the Pole.

questions.q: Stretch: Which route would you choose and why?
questions.a: Reasoned answer using distance, steepness and danger

questions.q: Big question: which route would you choose to reach the South Pole, and why?
questions.a: Reasoned answer comparing distance, features and dangers
